rapport_notes: Joanna is warm, patient, and responsive to the customer; good pacing and empathy around the antique furniture concern.
process_discipline_notes: No differentiators repeated; silences held appropriately after open-ended questions.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launches straight into confirmation and logistics ('this Friday, correct? The eleventh') without framing time or an ask upfront.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked late: 'Do you have any special instructions, concerns or stresser about this move or about moving in Al so you want me to take note of at this time' — after email, date, address, inventory, and room layout have all been probed.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised antique furniture concern. Rep dug: 'And sorry about that but yeah, I'll make sure to let the guys know on Friday.' Customer added detail about stacking and legs. Rep acknowledged and committed to briefing the crew — genuine two-layer follow-up on the single concern raised.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Covered in Stage 2 takeaway: 'I'll make sure to let the guys know on Friday' (damage care commitment) + 'we'll send you the names of the guys ahead of time' (Meet Your Mover).
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Covered in Stage 2: 'we'll send you the names of the guys ahead of time to let you know who's coming to help out with the move.'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Covered in Stage 2: 'And lastly on time guarantee if we run late we provide discounts by the end of the day.'
evidence_quotes.communication_not_covered: No mention of day-before call, named crew lead updates, or inbox communication anywhere in the call.
evidence_quotes.no_estimate_anchor: Pricing given ($220/hr, $550 minimum for Friday, $520 for Thursday) but no 'typical 2-person 4-hour move' framing or personalization anchor.
evidence_quotes.no_save_your_ass: None of the five Save Your Ass lines appear: no 'we commit to the rate' framing, no 'estimate is a window because your move is yours,' no 'if the crew beats it you pay less,' no self-prep tip, no 'does that feel fair' + silence.
evidence_quotes.no_rate_lock: Rep does not mention 'your rate locks when you book.'
evidence_quotes.close: Call ends with logistical confirmation ('we'll see you this coming Friday the eleventh') but no explicit closing ask ('would you like our help') and no rate-lock mention.

top_strength: Joanna handled the antique furniture concern with genuine two-layer follow-up and made a clear commitment to brief the crew, building trust on a pain point the customer had experienced before.
coaching_note: Skip the quid pro quo entirely and jump straight into logistics probing — this leaves the call feeling transactional rather than consultative; add a 30-second framing line at the top ('I'll ask a few quick questions to get us on the right track, should take about five minutes, then we'll lock in your rate') to reset the tone and reset Stage 1.
